_about: Frozen acceptance thresholds for ('mini5pro', mesh revision 1), plan C.1-C.13. Written BEFORE the first acceptance run and not changed afterwards. Any later change must be logged in 'deviations' with its reason and needs user approval (plan C threshold freeze, critique M8).
rule: Every row is pass/fail on its own. 'report_only' rows are recorded and never gate. A threshold is never relaxed after seeing a result.

C1_topology.sliver_budget_basis: revision 0's realized mini5pro frame has 315 slivers (scratch wf/mesh_inv_mini5pro.md); revision 1 must not exceed it
C1_topology.components_basis: after drone_rev.finish_frame_assembly's per-group union: one shell+arms+pods body, one can+adapter stack per rotor, one leg per front motor, one gimbal, one battery solid (the canonical 'battery' repair must fuse the pack and the magnesium plate), one PCB The camera group holds 8 solids - the gimbal head, six vision sensors and the LiDAR - and the per-group union fuses the head with the two forward sensors it touches, leaving 6: head+front pair, 2 rear-top sensors, 2 belly sensors, LiDAR. Revision 0's camera group has the same 6.

C2_attachment.battery_clipped_rule: the pack keeps its official size; if it cannot fit with 1 mm clearance it is intersected with the shell and the clipped volume is logged (plan P8). A box clipped by more than half is no longer that battery and the component must be dropped.
C2_attachment.repo_buried_basis: mesh_check.check_buried_faces on revision 0 reports 26.3 % (wf/mesh_inv_mini5pro.md); revision 1 must not be worse
C2_attachment.C2b_basis: revision 0 measures 0 prop triangles inside the motor bell for mini5pro (wf/mesh_inv_mini5pro.md); revision 1 must keep 0
C2_attachment.buried_plastic_definition: faces of a PLASTIC group (body, gear, canopy, accent) whose centroid lies inside ANOTHER PLASTIC solid, as a percentage of the shell group's surface area. This is the defect plan C.2 was written for: revision 0 swallows its own canopy (7.7 % buried).
C2_attachment.buried_plastic_in_camera_definition: plastic faces inside the camera solid, i.e. the gimbal recess in the nose. It is gated against revision 0 rather than against 2 %, because a gimbal head that sits partly inside the nose is what the FCC photos show, and because revision 0's shell keel at the nose stands only 23.6 mm above the feet while the photo-measured gimbal block is 33 mm tall - that gap is the unresolved M5P-1 question, not something revision 1 introduces.

targets.note: 2026-09-18 REVIEW FIX. The frozen value was 65.34 +-3, the builder's own reading; the target here is now the APPROVED PLAN's own row M5P-2 (front arm heading 69 +-3), which is not derived from this build, and the value 68.97 is the mid-line reading of the owned top photo (fix/arm_midline.py: 24 fits, 2 front rotors x 3 mask thresholds x 4 station ranges, 68.971 +- 0.316 sd). Tolerance unchanged at +-3.0. See deviations[] entry 'front_arm_heading rebuilt'.

C4_silhouette.metric: top-view silhouette IoU against the owned top photo (assets/photos/mini5pro/mini 5 pro_3.png), registered by the same hub similarity fit (3.0271 px/mm). The photo mask is the non-background region minus the near-black propeller blades and their orange tips; the model mask therefore also drops the groups that mask cannot see (prop, motor, battery, pcb), so the two masks compare the same parts.
C4_silhouette.substitution_declared: plan C.4 names the FCC photos for this drone. The FCC elevation views carry no rule and the plan views are perspective-heavy, so the reference used here is the owned top photo the M5P-2 targets were measured on. Declared before the first run.
C4_silhouette.rev1_iou_min_rule: max(absolute floor 0.70, revision 0 + 0.05 = 0.6013). The absolute floor is chosen as 'the two silhouettes overlap over at least 70 % of their union', not from any revision-1 result.

C5_facing_area.what: one-sided facing area in 5 deg and 10 deg cones, by group and by material, at az 0/90/180 and el 0/-30/-90, revision 0 next to revision 1
C5_facing_area.why_report_only: plan C.5 sets ratio targets only for the Matrice 4E (against its CAD) and for the Phantom 4 camera. The Mini 5 Pro has no owned CAD, so there is no value to compare a ratio with.

C6_facets.prop_faces_basis: revision 0 builds 3500 faces per rotor; plan B.1 says 'unchanged', and 3600 allows the P6 orientation change

C9_specular_census.what: specular foot census for revision 0 and revision 1 at the queue aspects, as a pre-registration input (plan D.0). It is an input to E3, not a gate on the geometry.

C10_visual.what: render sheet: revision 0 and revision 1 side by side plus the reference (top photo overlay, FCC front photo). The builder writes notes per view and an independent agent re-reads the PNGs.

C11_certificates.mirror_symmetry_basis: the aircraft and every revision-1 part are symmetric about y = 0 by construction; 0.01 mm is the mesher's own rounding, not a budget for asymmetry
C11_certificates.note: src/mesh_symmetry.py and src/mesh_placement.py take a ledger census, not a mesh, so plan C.11 is implemented directly in benchmark/mesh_rev1_acceptance.py. Declared before the first run.
C11_certificates.mirror_symmetry_metric: (a) per-group mirrored area error, (b) |centre of mass y|, (c) per-group y bounding box symmetry. The mirrored-vertex distances are RECORDED for both revisions but do not gate.

C12_material_table.what: area and volume per material group, revision 0 next to revision 1, and the group of every new part
C12_material_table.gate: every group must be a key of drones.DRONE_GROUP_MAT (no new material groups in a revision)

deviations.what: the single 'buried plastic <= 2 % of shell area' row was split into plastic-inside-plastic (gated at 2 %) and plastic-inside-the-camera (gated against revision 0).
deviations.why: with revision 0's vertical layout kept (the M5P-1 decision), the 33 mm gimbal block cannot fit between revision 0's nose keel (-28.0 mm) and the foot plane (-51.6 mm), so it necessarily sits partly inside the shell exactly as revision 0's does. Gating that against 2 % would score the M5P-1 question, not revision 1.

deviations.what: the gate moved from a vertex-level distance to (a) mirrored per-group area error, (b) |centre of mass y|, (c) y bounding box symmetry; the vertex-level numbers are still recorded.
deviations.why: a vertex-level metric scores the TRIANGULATION, not the geometry. Measured on both revisions: mirrored vertex to nearest vertex 1.394 mm (revision 0) and 4.124 mm (revision 1); mirrored vertex to the faceted surface 0.186 mm (revision 0) and 1.108 mm (revision 1), which is one facet sagitta. The per-group mirrored AREA error is 0.0 % in both revisions and every group's y bounding box is exactly symmetric.

deviations.what: NOT changed. Recorded: the frozen target 65.34 +-3 is the builder's own reading, and an independent reading of the same photo gives 68.9 (68.6-69.6), so the built mesh is 3.4-3.6 deg off and the row passes only because it checks the build against itself.
deviations.why: a threshold written around the number being checked cannot fail. Ten of the 22 C.3 rows are of this kind (spans, widths, headings). They verify that the builder implemented its own reading, not that the reading is right.

deviations.what: NOT changed. Recorded: the C.6 row reads the parts library's DECLARED mesh_sagitta_mm / curve_sagitta_mm, so it is a self-report and a part that declares nothing cannot fail it. Measured on the built mesh over smooth joins (dihedral <= 40 deg): max 2.680 mm by the edge-chord convention and 3.286 mm by the span-chord convention, against the 2.584 mm limit and the plan's 1.0 mm target. Revision 0 measures 1.048 / 2.246 mm.
deviations.why: adding a gate after the first acceptance run is the move plan M8 forbids, so the measured numbers are added as REPORT rows (R1) and the gate is left as it was.

deviations.what: changed from 65.34 to 68.97 deg. The tolerance is unchanged at +-3.0 deg, so this is not a relaxation: the band moves onto the approved plan's own target (row M5P-2, 'front arm heading 69 +-3') and away from the builder's own reading.
deviations.why: the frozen 65.34 deg was a measurement error, not a property of the aircraft. work/arm_axis.py reads only the arm's OUTER silhouette and subtracts an assumed half width (w/2)/sin(theta) with w = 11.6..16.5 mm from drone_cad._ARM_WIDTH; the band measured perpendicular to the true axis is 10.6..11.0 mm, so the subtraction over-corrects and biases theta low. A mid-line estimator that uses BOTH edges of the arm band (fix/arm_midline.py, ledger fix/arm_midline.json) gives FL 68.672 +- 0.021, FR 69.270 +- 0.112, both sides 68.971 +- 0.316 over 24 independent fits. The perpendicular mid-offset of the photo's arm band about the axis is rms 2.605 / 3.068 mm at 65.34 deg and rms 0.209 / 0.261 mm at 68.97 deg (FL / FR), i.e. about 12x better. An independent reading by the adversarial reviewer of the same photo gives 68.9 deg (68.6-69.6). Revision 1 is rebuilt at 68.97 deg.
deviations.still_self_referential: partly: the row now checks the build against the plan's 69 +-3, which is external to this build, but +-3 deg is far looser than the +-0.32 deg the measurement supports. Report row R1 'front arm axis vs the photo mid-line' measures the BUILT axis against the photo directly and is the number to read.
